title: He had money. Women. Projects. Wine. Applause.
paragraphs:
He had money. Women. Projects. Wine. Applause.
And at the end of it all, Solomon said: “Meaningless.”
That’s Ecclesiastes 2.

We think the next thing will finally quiet the ache.
More success.
More pleasure.
More recognition.
More proof that our life matters.
But Ecclesiastes 2 drags that lie into the light.

Solomon chased laughter. It didn’t satisfy.
He chased pleasure. It slipped through his fingers.
He built houses, planted vineyards, gathered wealth, multiplied possessions, and became greater than those before him. Yet when he looked at everything he had achieved, he called it vanity—a vapor, a mist, something you cannot hold (Ecclesiastes 2:10–11).

That is the heartbreak of life without God at the center.
You can fill your hands and still starve in your soul.

Ecclesiastes is not telling you that work is worthless, or that joy is evil.
It is telling you that nothing created can carry the weight of being your savior.

Not pleasure.
Not ambition.
Not romance.
Not legacy.
Not even your own wisdom.

Because meaning is not found in what you can gain under the sun.
Meaning is found in the God who rules above it.
This is where grace walks in.

Jesus stepped into our empty chasing.
He met restless people like us—people exhausted from trying to build a life big enough to save themselves. And He did not offer another distraction. He offered Himself.

The world says, “Consume more.”
Christ says, “Come to Me.”

The world says, “Prove your worth.”
Christ says, “It is finished.”

The world says, “Chase meaning.”
Jesus says, “I am the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14:6).

Ecclesiastes 2 is a warning, yes.
But it is also mercy.
Because the collapse of false meaning is often the beginning of true surrender.

So if everything you chased left you hollow, do not waste that pain.
Let it bring you to Christ.
Repent. Return. Receive grace.
The life you were trying to manufacture can only be given by Jesus.
From vanity to victory. From empty hands to a full heart in Christ.
